title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Booking Status in Telex Release Charging
content:
Charging a telex release on a `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` record takes account of the booking behind the document. This page defines when that booking stands far enough along for the charge.

## Rule

1. The booking stands far enough along when its status is loaded, departed or closed.
2. At gated in it also stands far enough along, provided the document's type carries the received-for-shipment permission.
3. Only a booking held by the documentation party of the document is read. A booking held by any other customer is never read for the charge, and the release is then treated as not having taken place.
4. A booking in any other status does not stand far enough along, and without such a booking the release is not treated as having taken place for charging.

## Hypothetical readings

- Own booking shown as departed, on any type: far enough along.
- Own booking shown as gated in, on a type permitted to issue received-for-shipment: far enough along; the same status on a type without that permission: not far enough along.
- Own booking still confirmed or merely with equipment released: not far enough along.
- Booking of another customer, even one shown as loaded: never read, so the release is not treated as having taken place.

## Point of judgement

**The booking has been closed after the voyage. Does the charge still see it as far enough along?** Yes. Closed counts.
